## `managed-deepagents-sdk/`

The [Managed Deep Agents SDK](https://github.com/langchain-ai/managed-deepagents-sdk) at the commit in `UPSTREAM`: the `mda` CLI's Rust source (`crates/`) and the `managed-deepagents` Python runtime (`packages/pypi/`). `mda/` installs the runtime from here (an editable uv path source), and `make mda-cli` builds the CLI with `cargo` into that runtime's `_binaries/`, where its `mda` command runs it from. `mda build` and `mda deploy` bundle this runtime into the deployment, so what runs is exactly this tree.

The SDK's `main` is vendored, and `UPSTREAM` records the exact commit the tree comes from (full SHA, then its date, then its branch when that is not `main`). While Open SWE needs SDK work that hasn't reached `main`, such as the Linear and GitHub channels on the `mda/0.10` release branch, it vendors that branch with `--branch`; once the branch lands, a plain update moves it back to `main`. Our changes are edits in the tree itself, as on a vendor branch: change the SDK by editing its files here, and review the change as an ordinary diff. `scripts/vendor.py` manages the rest:

- `uv run scripts/vendor.py` updates to the head of upstream `main`; `uv run scripts/vendor.py <sha>` updates to that commit, and refuses one that is not on `main`; `uv run scripts/vendor.py --branch <branch> [<sha>]` takes that upstream branch's head, or a commit on it, instead. When that commit doesn't build on the recorded one, as when moving from `main` to a release branch, the merge's base is where the two meet, so what the recorded commit has and the new one lacks stays, as our change with a note in `mda-changes/`. Files we left alone take upstream's new version. Into files we changed, it three-way merges upstream's changes (`git merge-file`, base: the recorded commit), and stops with conflict markers where both sides changed the same lines. Then it records the commit in `UPSTREAM` and relocks `mda/`.
- `uv run scripts/vendor.py --pr <n>` carries upstream pull request `<n>` before it reaches `main`, to try it in Open SWE first: it three-way merges the pull request's changes into the tree (base: where it branched off its base branch) and records it in [`mda-upstream-prs`](mda-upstream-prs), one per line: its number, the head commit carried, then its title. Run it again once the pull request has moved on, and it merges in what changed since the head carried. Once an update reaches a commit the pull request was merged into, it leaves `mda-upstream-prs`. Pull requests are looked up with `gh`.
- `uv run scripts/vendor.py --diff` prints our changes, carried pull requests included: the tree against `UPSTREAM`'s commit. Once upstream has one of them, the next update drops it from that list.

Every change we make there ourselves has a dated note in [`mda-changes/`](mda-changes/README.md): what changed, why Open SWE needs it, and what MDA needs before we can drop it. A carried pull request needs none: `mda-upstream-prs` names it, and the pull request says the rest.
